boards.title: Your First Weekend at Kettering University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A practical Saturday-to-Sunday sequence for learning Kettering’s campus anchors, getting active, and exploring public destinations in Flint.

cards.title: Start at Thompson Hall
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning: settle in and learn your residence hall
cards.notes: Locate the front desk, identify your unit’s common spaces, and save the Residence Life contact before heading across campus.
cards.short_summary: Begin the weekend by learning the layout and support point of Kettering’s first-year residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering identifies Thompson Hall as its centrally located residence hall and says it has four floors, two courtyards, and a lobby with puzzles, board games, televisions, and video games.
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall access is for residents and authorized guests; follow current Residence Life and guest procedures.

cards.title: Map Out the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning: find the campus collaboration hub
cards.notes: Walk the open floors, note where group work can happen, and choose a clear meeting point your new classmates can find easily.
cards.short_summary: Use a first circuit of the Learning Commons to establish an easy campus rendezvous.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering describes the Learning Commons as a technology-enriched building for collaboration, studying, socializing, and dining.
cards.access_notes: Campus facility; use is subject to current university building access and posted hours.

cards.title: Find the Knowledge Bars
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning: learn where library help lives
cards.notes: Stop at the third-floor service point, identify how to request research help, and bookmark the library site for off-campus access.
cards.short_summary: Turn a quick library-services introduction into a resource you can use throughout the term.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering says two Knowledge Bars in the Learning Commons host its digital library, whose resources are available to students on and off campus.
cards.access_notes: The Knowledge Bars are in the Learning Commons; in-person service follows current library and building hours.

cards.title: Browse the Saturday Market
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday: explore a year-round Flint destination
cards.notes: Walk the vendor aisles before choosing whether to buy anything, and use the published vendor map to keep a group together.
cards.short_summary: Make the public market a flexible midday stop that works for browsing or lunch.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flint Farmers’ Market describes itself as a year-round public market with more than 50 vendors and lists Saturday hours of 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: About The Market - Flint Farmers' Market
cards.access_notes: Current published market hours are Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; holiday changes are possible.

cards.title: Choose a Gallery at the FIA
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon: add visual art to the sequence
cards.notes: Pick one gallery rather than rushing the full museum, carry student identification, and confirm admission eligibility at the desk.
cards.short_summary: Use a focused gallery visit as a change of pace after the market.
cards.evidence_claim: The Flint Institute of Arts ticketing page lists museum hours, student admission, and free admission for Genesee County residents.
cards.access_notes: Published hours are 10 a.m.–5 p.m. Saturday. Admission is free for Genesee County residents; others should check current ticket prices.

cards.entity_name: Connie and Jim John Recreation Center
cards.title: Take a Recreation-Center Lap
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon: learn the student fitness options
cards.notes: Check in at the front desk, tour only permitted areas, and choose one low-pressure activity suited to your ability and equipment.
cards.short_summary: Learn where Kettering students can swim, walk, exercise, and join recreational sports.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering says the private Recreation Center serves its students, faculty, staff, and their families and includes courts, a track, fitness rooms, and a pool.
cards.access_notes: This is a private university facility. Bring student identification and check current facility, pool, and activity hours before visiting.

cards.title: See Atwood from the Outside
cards.subtitle: Saturday early evening: identify Kettering’s stadium
cards.notes: Use the public exterior and signage as your orientation point; enter only for an authorized event or university activity.
cards.short_summary: Recognize the stadium and its role in Kettering recreation without assuming open entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering identifies Atwood Stadium as an 11,000-seat venue in Flint’s Carriage Town district used by university recreation and community sports programs.
cards.source_title: Kettering University's Atwood Stadium | Kettering University
cards.access_notes: Stadium entry depends on scheduled events, programs, or reservations; this card recommends only a public exterior orientation stop.

cards.title: Follow a Chevy Commons Trail
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening: take a daylight riverfront walk
cards.notes: Stay on the designated pedestrian trail, visit with a companion, and turn back before daylight or weather conditions deteriorate.
cards.short_summary: Close Saturday outdoors on a documented public trail near Kettering’s side of Flint.
cards.evidence_claim: Genesee County Parks describes Chevy Commons as a public park created from a former industrial site with trails for pedestrians and bicyclists.
cards.access_notes: Use designated public trails in daylight and follow all posted park notices, closures, and construction detours.

cards.title: Reset on the Rooftop Terrace
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning: begin with an outdoor study-space check
cards.notes: Bring a notebook, test where the outlets and shaded seats are, and leave promptly if the terrace is closed or weather shifts.
cards.short_summary: Start Sunday by identifying an outdoor place that can support both breaks and light study.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering documents a 1,600-square-foot Rooftop Terrace with seating, green space, hammocks, and electrical outlets in the Learning Commons.
cards.access_notes: Terrace access depends on Learning Commons hours, weather, and any posted university restrictions.

cards.title: Finish at Sloan Museum
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon: explore Flint science and history
cards.notes: Choose one hands-on gallery, bring student identification and proof of residency if applicable, and allow time for the return trip.
cards.short_summary: End the sequence with an interactive introduction to Flint’s science and local-history collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Sloan Museum’s official visitor page lists hands-on science and history galleries, Sunday hours of noon to 5 p.m., and admission terms for residents and nonresidents.
cards.source_title: Hours & Tickets | Sloan Museum of Discovery
cards.access_notes: Current published Sunday hours are noon–5 p.m. Genesee County residents receive free general admission with proof; other visitors need tickets.
